Hi, I'm Cameron Kuey. I sold candy bars in high school, and I've been building things ever since: businesses, stories, and lately, the systems and software that help teams do their best work.

Today I'm the Director of Business Operations at Doodle Pirates Foundation, a nonprofit that trains neurodivergent adults in real-world work skills. I design how the organization runs, then build the tools that run it. That includes four connected Airtable bases, about 20 AI agents mapped to roles across six departments, and an internal dashboard I took from concept to production in under two weeks as product owner, building with Claude Code and Claude Design and reviewing every change. You can read how that came together in the Internal Dashboard case study.

Before that, I spent four years at Modern Health. As a Creative Producer I ran scheduling, logistics, and live production for 570+ provider-led group sessions. As Content Operations Manager I built 150+ automations across Zapier, Airtable, Salesforce, Quickbase, and Google Apps Script, working with Revenue Operations, Product, Marketing, Clinical, Finance, and Legal to turn messy requirements into systems that worked.

I started out as a storyteller. In 2012 I founded Cosie Co., a photo and video company that grew from solo freelancing to a 10-year business serving 200+ clients. In 2015 I founded The Cultivation Project, a faith-based nonprofit media organization, and led it as Executive Director through 2022, directing a 10+ person team that produced 100+ documentaries, promotional videos, and podcast episodes. I've also given keynotes and led workshops on video production and storytelling, including a four-week filmmaking bootcamp in 2020.

The thread through all of it: I love telling stories, solving hard problems, and finding better ways to get information from one place to another.

pages.title: The Money Maker App
pages.oldTitle: Cameron Kuey - The Money Maker App

blocks.html:
Context

Our modern digital society makes handling our finances easier than ever, but there is still no perfect all-in-one app that allows us to invest, manage our finances, serves as our bank, and let's us send and receive money instantly. Imagine if Robinhood, Mint, and Venmo all merged into an intuitive platform.

Goal

The Money Maker App is designed to be a single platform in which people can manage their finances, invest their money, and send & receive payments.

How it Works (try it)

I designed the app to minimize the overwhelming complexity of financial information and numbers, and package that information into a mobile screen in which anyone with a high school education can understand.

Each screen serves a unique purpose in helping the user understand specific information related to their money that is tied up in a certain way. The amount of information a bank statement or brokerage account can be very overwhelming, which is every category of information has its own label and drop down arrow to allow the user to hide that section at will.

The search screen allows the user to find information on any stock or cryptocurrency, while also showing them any of their past or current trades related to that stock or cryptocurrency. A user can simply add the stock or cryptocurrency to their main watchlist, or press the "trade" button to open or close a position.

The watchlist screen acts as a hub for all stocks and cryptocurrencies that the user wants to follow on a daily basis. This hub will constantly refresh to show the latest prices of all followed assets.

The investment screen makes it clear about what the value of the user's investment account is, how much cash they have available to trade, and what assets they already own. They can simply click on any stock, option, or cryptocurrency that they own to see more details about that asset. Since this screen only shows what the user already owns, it will prevent more mistakes and confusion for the user.

At any given moment, the user can click on the trading icon to trade a stock, option or cryptocurrency. Once again, this was designed to make trading as clear and transparent as possible. The user can select all of the aspects of the trade, such as what order type they want, how many they want to buy/sell, and how long they want the order to stay active. Level II data is also built into the trading screen so that users can see a live feed of bids and asks, giving them all of the tools needed to make the best investment decisions.

The accounts icon gives the user a live calculation of all assets, an easy to understand graph showing their money in and out flows, and instant management of all cash and credit accounts. Users can transfer money between accounts and investments, use the built in Zelle, and/or pay bills all within the same app. Since the information is organized clearly and simply, the user will always have the most accurate picture of what their financial situation is like.

blocks.html:
Problem

There is no single, secure platform for missionaries to fundraise and share updates with supporters. Missionaries want to spend less time creating newsletters, email blasts, and taking care of mailing lists, and more time doing the work they were called to do.

Goal

Klema exists to provide missionaries with a single platform to efficiently write updates, grow partnerships, and fundraise with supporters around the world. Klema also acts as a one-stop-shop for every missionary & ministry that a person supports.

How it Works (try it)

I designed the app to be intuitive from both a supporter's perspective as well as a missionaries' perspective. As a missionary, they can simply click the "+" button on the bottom navigation bar to instantly write a prayer request (almost like a status update), blog post, create a community, or start a fundraiser.

As a supporter (or follower), the main content feed shows all of the latest blog posts, fundraisers, and prayer requests from people who they choose to follow. Supporters have the option to "like", add to a journal (to save for later), and instantly comment or donate if they choose.

The best part of working on the Klema iOS app design was the ability to talk to missionaries to get their feedback and implement changes instantly. I had the opportunity to present Klema to a room full of people to gather instant feedback and impressions.

blocks.html: I designed the website, graphics and logos for The Cultivation Project, which is intended to be viewed by donors and partner organizations. The Cultivation Project works on variety of multimedia projects that need a home for donors and supporters to find.

The Project:

For The Cultivation Project's 5th anniversary, I made a special newsletter that broke down the various milestones and major projects that were achieved over the years. Since The Cultivation Project is mainly funded by individual donors, it is important to design and communicate as simply as possible so that every donor can understand what is going on at any given time. I designed each page to emphasize one major milestone or project that was achieved, and when together, create a timeline of The Cultivation Project's history. I designed every page using Adobe InDesign.

Annual Report for The Cultivation Project - Keynote Presentation

This is an example of a keynote presentation that I put together for The Cultivation Project's annual board meeting. The purpose of this presentation is to provide the board with a general summary of the milestones achieved during the year, a review of the financial situation of the organization, a roadmap of the upcoming year, and a budget for the upcoming year to vote on. These meetings usually consist of a lot of talking and information sharing, so having easy-to-read and clear slides makes the experience a lot better for the board.

The Cultivation project's Flow Chart

I created this flow chart to help The Cultivation Project's team and support base understand the roles and purpose of each project that is being worked on within the organization. Before this chart, it would get really confusing for people to understand the many different divisions, project names, and purposes that each aspect had toward the overall mission.
